summary: Instagram is doing most of the work: nearly every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 50 views. The best videos are about robots and common sensors, with a surprising or curious first line. Videos on everyday gadgets like taps, doors and smoke alarms, and repeated topics like IR and smoke sensors, get much less attention.
winningPattern: Instagram-first Hindi Shorts about robots or simple sensor tricks (clap switch, gyro, line follower, IR robot). The title opens with a surprising claim or a 'cannot-do' twist (e.g. 'Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', 'Ke Paas Dimaag Nahi Hota', 'Ke Bina Gir Jaata'), is short, and promises one clear secret. Robot or maker-project visuals get more likes, saves and shares than public-place gadgets (mall door, lift, washroom tap).
doMore: Make robot and maker-project explainers (balancing, obstacle avoidance, line following) with a bold, counter-intuitive title
Use the 'X doesn't have Y, yet it does Z' title style that worked for Clap Switch and Line Follower
Post Instagram first and add a save/share prompt, since saves and shares come from project-style videos
Test a different title and thumbnail on YouTube, since the same Hindi videos get almost no views there
End with a quick 'build it yourself' hint with an Arduino module to boost saves
stopDoing: Making several near-duplicate videos on the same sensor (IR, smoke, automatic tap) within days
Generic question titles about public-place gadgets like mall doors, lifts and washroom taps
Posting English videos without a plan, since the one English upload only reached 161 YouTube views and nothing on Instagram
